web-global-guide-taste-of-your-world.ima: Creator with a colourful headwrap and camera on lavender paper
web-global-guide-taste-of-your-world.pro: Share one small, real part of your world through a personal exchange.
web-global-guide-taste-of-your-world.aud: Food, language, travel and craft creators who enjoy explaining their own lived experience.
web-global-guide-taste-of-your-world.int: The everyday detail you take for granted may be exactly what someone else is curious about. Offer a focused exchange: the story of a family recipe, a beginner language conversation or a demonstration of your own craft. Speak from your experience rather than presenting one perspective as an entire culture.
web-global-guide-taste-of-your-world.pre: Choose one clearly named topic. A recipe conversation, language practice and a craft lesson require different expectations and materials.
Ask what the guest hopes to learn and which language you will use. Share an optional ingredient or materials list in advance if needed.
Prepare a small object, photograph or demonstration you have permission to share. Keep your home location and other people’s private stories off camera.
web-global-guide-taste-of-your-world.age: Ask what drew the guest to the topic and confirm the scope of the exchange.
Share a specific story or skill
Explain one recipe tradition, practise a short conversation or demonstrate one craft technique.
Invite questions and make room for the guest’s perspective without assumptions about their background.
Recap a phrase, technique or story and explain any resource you agreed to share.
web-global-guide-taste-of-your-world.inv: A 30-minute conversation about the food stories I grew up with, including a walkthrough of one family recipe. No cooking experience needed. This is a personal cultural exchange, not a nutrition consultation.
web-global-guide-taste-of-your-world.bou: Describe your own experience without claiming to represent every person in a country or community. Credit cultural sources and collaborators.
For food or craft demonstrations, explain relevant practical precautions and material limitations. Do not provide health advice or promise allergen safety.
web-global-guide-taste-of-your-world.fol: Share the agreed recipe notes, phrase list or craft references with proper attribution. Ask which part sparked their curiosity and use that feedback to shape a specific next offering.
